title: Discovery of New Zintl Films and Nanowires Grown by Topotaxy Conversion of III-V Semiconductors
authors: Man Suk Song, Lothar Houben, Jean Souza, Edanel Fishbein, Moshe Haim, Ambikesh Gupta, Yufei Zhao, Anna-Eden Kossoy, Binghai Yan, Haim Beidenkopf, Hadas Shtrikman
abstract: Zintl phases draw broad interest for their diverse structural, magnetic, thermoelectric, topological and optical properties. Recently, Zintl Eu$_3$In$_2$As$_4$ and Eu$_5$In$_2$As$_6$ nanowires with axion magneto-topology have been synthesized by molecular beam epitaxy via topotactic conversion of InAs wurtzite and zincblende nanowires. Here we extend this methodology, demonstrating that topotaxial mutual-exchange growth applies not only to a broader set of III-V semiconductors beyond InAs but also to three-dimensional substrates whose surfaces are converted into Zintl thin films, as well as to nanowires. We report the growth of two new compounds: Eu$_5$Ga$_2$As$_6$ thin films converted from GaAs substrates, and Eu$_5$Al$_2$As$_6$ thin films from AlAs films. We also convert GaAs nanowires of both wurtzite and zincblende structures into Eu$_5$Ga$_2$As$_6$ nanowires. Though the stoichiometry is the same as in the previously reported Eu$_5$In$_2$As$_6$ case, microscopy and diffraction reveal a single-phase Pnma symmetry group rather than Pbam, highlighting symmetry-guided topotactic pathways to new Zintl frameworks. The compounds host an intricate magnetic phase diagram with three magnetic transitions, including two distinct antiferromagnetic orders and a canted antiferromagnetic phase that evolves into another antiferromagnetic phase under applied field through a spin-flop transition. Ab initio calculations predict that both Zintls are semiconductors with gaps of 0.79 eV in Eu$_5$Ga$_2$As$_6$ and 0.90 eV in Eu$_5$Al$_2$As$_6$. The lower symmetry and increased structural complexity suggest suppressed lattice thermal conductivity, pointing to thermoelectric potential alongside prospects in spintronics and detector technologies. These results give an epitaxy-compatible route for discovering and integrating magnetic Zintl thin films and nanowires directly from relevant III-V semiconductors.
summary: This work reports the successful synthesis of novel Zintl compounds, Eu5Ga2As6 and Eu5Al2As6, by growing them epitaxially from III-V semiconductor substrates. The research characterizes their unique crystal structures, complex magnetic ordering, and semiconducting nature, establishing a new, scalable route for creating functional magnetic thin films and nanowires.
main_problem: The research aims to discover and synthesize new Zintl films and nanowires by extending the topotactic conversion methodology from III-V semiconductors.
main_result: Two new Zintl compounds, Eu5Ga2As6 and Eu5Al2As6, were successfully grown, exhibiting complex magnetic ordering and predicted semiconductor gaps suitable for spintronics and thermoelectric applications.
method: The study combines experimental techniques like Molecular Beam Epitaxy (MBE), STEM-HAADF imaging, and magnetic measurements with theoretical predictions from *ab initio* calculations.
model_or_system: The physical system involves Zintl phases, which are synthesized by converting the crystal structure of parent III-V semiconductors (like GaAs or AlAs) into the desired Zintl framework.
key_observables: Crystal structure (Pnma space group), electronic band gaps (0.79 eV and 0.90 eV), magnetic transitions (AFM, CAFM, spin-flop), and growth morphology (thin films and nanowires).
important_parameters: The stoichiometry of the new compounds (Eu5M2As6), the applied magnetic field strength, and the substrate orientation are key parameters.
main_assumptions: The growth process is assumed to be topotactic, meaning the new structure is guided by the underlying crystal lattice of the parent semiconductor.
figures_summary: Figures show SEM/STEM images detailing the growth morphology and interface structure on various GaAs substrates, XRD scans confirming the Pnma structure, and M-H/M-T curves mapping the complex magnetic phase diagram.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the methodology (topotactic conversion), then characterizing the growth on different substrates (morphology and structure), followed by detailed analysis of the electronic and magnetic properties, and concluding with potential applications.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state materials, the study of magnetic phase transitions (AFM/CAFM) and the coupling between structure and magnetism touches upon concepts relevant to correlated electron systems and emergent quantum phenomena in condensed matter.
